top_band: terracotta/red-brown tiled roof slope from row 2 to row 43 (lightest at the ridge rows 3-12, graduating darker down to row 42, with a front roof edge trim at row 42-43)
evidence: Reading down a middle column: rows 2-43 show the angled top surface of the tiled roof (41 rows tall) with a distinct lighter ridge cap at rows 3-8 and a front edge trim at rows 42-43. Below it, rows 44-45 carry a 2-row eave shadow on the plaster wall, and rows 44-78 form the vertical front wall (35 rows) with a recessed arched doorway (dark inner shadow along the arch at row 54) and window.

style.evidence: The roof uses 6 terracotta shading steps with per-tile highlights and dark red-brown outlines, and the plaster wall has a 4-5 step beige speckle with eave shadow. However, compared to the Beodeul reference buildings, the roof tiles are larger and blockier (4x4 blocks rather than fine 2x3 overlapping scales), the timber framing lacks diagonal braces and fine wood grain, and the door/window/chimney use simpler geometric fills with less micro-detail per 16x16 tile.
